parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national passport/entry rules force sex-assigned-at-birth markers and allow refusal or fraud findings for document discrepancies; division law mandates birth-certificate sex in covered restrooms and was enforced by ID checks, with trespass arrest elsewhere. Facilities exclusion is a universal state-imposed exposure in covered government buildings, and custody records show conversion practices and abuse. National hate-crime coverage and litigation/injunctions are partial protections, but no working remedy is documented for a visitor stopped at a covered facility or border. Street-violence data are too ambiguous to establish a trans-specific rate. Baseline outed-adult risk is high but not catastrophic: no execution and imprisonment is not routine unless detained. Minors face care bans and school-hostile rules.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules require sex assigned at birth on passports/visas; X markers halted; cable allows refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiry; litigation ongoing; legal-aid FAQ. No visitor-facing guarantee against refusal.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport with X or mismatch can trigger secondary screening or refusal, then immigration detention.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse of trans men; corrections practices include conversion therapy, hormone removal and denial of care.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute and some court injunctions; no documented effective custody remedy for visitors.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at the border can lead to immigration custody, where documented abuse applies.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division statute requires restrooms match birth-certificate sex in public schools, universities, prisons and state buildings; fines; ID checks; criminal trespass in some states; national order bars congruent federal facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some private venues not covered; courts have enjoined some national measures; state ID checks admitted women with female markers.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor in a covered building may be ID-checked; refusal to leave can become trespass; national facilities policy adds federal buildings.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors; national rules restrict funding/public insurance and describe minor care as mutilation; adult visitor continuity is not specified.
care_services.protection: Injunctions block some national measures; emergency care is not shown denied to adult visitors.
care_services.interaction: Travelling with a trans minor raises care-denial and school/legal exposure; adult visitor medication continuity is uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritizes 'radically pro-transgender' groups; justice reward guidance references 'radical gender ideology'; division parental-rights law mandates deadnaming in schools.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy says powers will not target mere disagreement; courts have blocked several orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Visitor activism or visible advocacy could attract scrutiny; ordinary tourism is less directly targeted.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans care for trans minors; schools must deadname and misgender; parental-rights statute bars discussion; national order threatens prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition.
minors_guardians.protection: Some injunctions and local policies; no visitor-specific protection documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces facility rules, care denial and school/legal hostility; a guardian may be investigated.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime law excludes gender identity; no statewide nondiscrimination; LGB visibility rolled back; trans-specific violence rate for the division is not established.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; local ordinances exist in some cities; police enforced bathroom law rather than protecting.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: An outed visitor reporting assault may face uneven local recourse; no documented pattern of police protection for trans victims.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Visitor has no clear remedy against border refusal, facility arrest or custody abuse; state definition act bars marker changes.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National litigation, injunctions, legal-aid FAQ and some court rulings; not shown to reverse visitor harms in practice.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are slow and post-hoc; border and facility decisions happen before effective relief.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar entry-exclusion and stranding risk, but this dossier adds enforced facility exclusion and documented custody abuse; hence lower.
0.55-B is administrative secondary screening and refusal without routine facility criminal enforcement. Here ID checks, trespass exposure and custody harm make it materially lower.
0.75-C has trained border officers, tribunal appeals and working remedies. Here litigation is partial and facilities/entry rules operate before relief; much lower.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines a restrictive national document/entry posture with a division facilities law enforced by ID checks and criminal trespass. The heaviest exposures are universal in covered government buildings and at the border; custody abuse is severe but conditional on detention. Legal challenges and national hate-crime coverage are real but do not provide a working remedy at the point of encounter. Street violence remains too ambiguously documented to drive the score. Compared with anchors, this sits below administrative-friction states and above catastrophic-execution states. Minors and guardians face additional care and school-related exposure.
